# Known-broken cross-language pairs whose dual-spec assertions FAIL by
# design. Listed bidders are excluded from the round-trip CI's blocking
# rules; their failures are reported as informational.
#
# One bidder name per line. Lines starting with # are comments; blank
# lines are ignored. Bidders are matched case-sensitively against the
# `bidder_name` field of the cross-language-pairs/<name>.dual-spec-
# assertions.yaml file.
#
# When to add a bidder here:
# - The dual-spec assertion file declares severity:fail on >=1 key, AND
# - The failure is a documented reality (e.g., aax: Java omits minLength:1)
#   that we're choosing to track via the assertion rather than fix
#
# When to remove a bidder:
# - The upstream divergence has been resolved (e.g., a future PR fixes
#   the schema gap) and the assertion file's severity drops to warn or
#   pass
#
# EVERY entry needs an expiry. Exclusions here downgrade a hard failure to
# informational, so without one a downgrade added for a specific reason
# outlives the reason and nobody notices. Immediately above each bidder
# line, add a directive:
#
#     # review-by: YYYY-MM-DD <bidder> — <what has to be true to remove it>
#
# `scripts/tests/test_accepted_warnings.py` (TestKnownBrokenPairs) fails
# once the date passes, and fails if an entry has no directive at all. On
# expiry: re-check whether the divergence still exists. If it is fixed,
# delete the entry; if it is not, push the date out and say what changed.
# Directives are comments, so the `grep -vE '^\s*(#|$)'` that builds the
# --allow-known-broken-pairs list is unaffected.

# review-by: 2027-02-18 aax — remove once the Java bidder-params schema
# gains `minLength: 1` on cid/crid, which is the divergence the dual-spec
# assertion declares severity:fail. Re-check against upstream
# prebid-server-java at that date; extend with a note if still open.
aax
